extracted.intended_audience: students, critics, and practitioners of art, poetry, and literary aesthetics
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and aesthetic standards for producing and judging painting, sculpture, and poetry with emphasis on the Hellenic ideal (breadth, unity, restraint) and on how modern art can adapt those ideals to complex modern experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hellenic breadth and generality
rubrics_metrics.description: Hellenic breadth and generality come of a culture minute, severe, constantly renewed, rectifying and concentrating its impressions into certain pregnant types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This breadth is not laxity; it derives from disciplined, concentrated culture. Evaluate works for a centrality and universality that distil many impressions into pregnant, exemplary types rather than diffuse or flaccid generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power to conceive humanity in a new, striking way
rubrics_metrics.description: The base of all artistic genius is the power of conceiving humanity in a new, striking, rejoicing way, of putting a happy world of its own creation in place of the meaner world of common days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the artist invents an imaginative world or tone that transforms ordinary life into something freshly significant; look for selection, transformation, and recombination of images by an imaginative intellect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and development of special situation (poetry & painting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting and poetry can accomplish their function in the choice and development of some special situation, which lifts or glorifies a character, in itself not poetical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good poetry/painting locates a 'focus' moment in which otherwise trivial or unlovely characters are made ideal by situation. Example: Robert Browning's poems (poetry of situations). Anti-pattern: failing to define or discriminate the moment so the situation does not 'find' the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of cunning, subordinate detail and atmosphere (painting)
rubrics_metrics.description: To realise this situation the artist has to employ the most cunning detail, to complicate and refine upon thought and passion a thousand-fold... power of indirect expression, of subordinate but significant detail, its atmosphere, its foregrounds and backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate painting by how it uses detailed, indirect means—textures, foreground/background relationships, atmospheric effects—to make a situation intelligible and emotionally resonant rather than by blatant didacticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purged, suggestive poetic language
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry requires language in its most purged form, its remote associations and suggestions, its double and treble lights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess poetic diction for economy (purging), suggestiveness (remote associations), and layered meanings (double/treble lights). Poetry should depend on suggestive compression rather than explicit exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sculptural emphasis on type and abstraction from detail
rubrics_metrics.description: In sculpture not the special situation, but the type, the general character of the subject to be delineated, is all-important... This it effects not by accumulation of detail, but by abstracting from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge sculpture by its ability to present broad, central, incisive lines and exemplary types; evaluate how incidental detail is removed to heighten the universal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of limitation / restraint of passion (Hellenic ideal)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a law of limitation; it keeps passion always below that degree of intensity at which it must necessarily be transitory... It allows passion to play lightly over the surface of the individual form, losing thereby nothing of its central impassivity, its depth and repose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong works preserve a controlled intensity—passion is present but restrained so as not to become transitory or one-note. Anti-patterns include overwrought emphasis, single-note fury, or fixed mask-like expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of the grotesque and one-sided types
rubrics_metrics.description: All such instances may be ranged under the grotesque; and the Hellenic ideal has nothing in common with the grotesque... faces fixed immovably into blank types of placid reverie.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of portraying characters as single, exaggerated qualities (grotesque masks) or frozen one-emotion types; such one-sidedness diminishes artistic depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of represented action / suggestion of motion
rubrics_metrics.description: The actions selected are those which would be without significance, except in a divine person—binding on a sandal or preparing for the bath... When a more complex and significant action is permitted, it is most often represented as just finished, so that eager expectancy is excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether action is suggested subtly (reserve) rather than depicted as dramatic movement; prefer moments of poised completion or quiet antecedent/after-effect to eager expectancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstraction of accidental, distracting detail
rubrics_metrics.description: All that is accidental, all that distracts the simple effect upon us of the supreme types of humanity, all traces in them of the commonness of the world, it gradually purges away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good work removes incidental particulars that distract from the essential, concentrating attention on central form or idea; judge how effectively the artist abstracts to present the type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colourless, unclassified purity and universality
rubrics_metrics.description: This colourless, unclassified purity of life... is the highest expression of that indifference which lies beyond all that is relative or partial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work attains a universality or purity that transcends local or transient colourings—work that feels like an 'immortal presentment' rather than a passing, particularised scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexless or morally neutral modelling
rubrics_metrics.description: The beauty of the Greek statues was a sexless beauty; the statues of the gods had the least traces of sex. Here there is a moral sexlessness... yet with a true beauty and significance of its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether depictions avoid reduction to sexual or moral particularity, thereby achieving a universal, idealized human form (appropriate to Hellenic modelling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serene handling of the sensuous (Heiterkeit)
rubrics_metrics.description: One result of this temperament is a serenity—Heiterkeit—which characterises Winckelmann's handling of the sensuous side of Greek art... This serenity is... the absence of any sense of want, or corruption, or shame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the artist's calm, unashamed handling of sensuous elements—sensuality treated with composure and purity rather than fever or guilt. Anti-pattern: sensuousness portrayed as intoxication or moral corruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detachment from intoxication by sensuousness
rubrics_metrics.description: From this intoxication Winckelmann is free; he fingers those pagan marbles with unsinged hands, with no sense of shame or loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic ideal: immerse thought in sensuous form without being consumed by it. Judge whether the creator maintains intellectual distance while exploiting sensuous appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of antique blitheness with modern complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Can the blitheness and universality of the antique ideal be communicated to artistic productions, which shall contain the fulness of the experience of the modern world?... What modern art has to do in the service of culture is so to rearrange the details of modern life, so to reflect it, that it may satisfy the spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess attempts to fuse Hellenic unity/serenity with the complexity of modern life—successful works rearrange modern particulars to restore a sense of balance and satisfy the intellectual need for completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of literary form to command variety and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us understand by poetry all literary production which attains the power of giving pleasure by its form, as distinct from its matter. Only in this varied literary form can art command that width, variety, delicacy of resources...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge literary works by formal mastery (structure, tone, language) that provides the necessary variety and subtlety to address modern conditions; form itself should be a source of pleasure and resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining sense of freedom within modern necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: What does the spirit need in the face of modern life? The sense of freedom... The chief factor in the thoughts of the modern mind concerning itself is the intricacy, the universality of natural law... Can art represent men and women in these bewildering toils so as to give the spirit at least an equivalent for the sense of freedom?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a work, while acknowledging determinism/complex natural laws, still offers readers/viewers an emotional or intellectual sense of freedom—often by the tragic/epic framing of situations that dignify human response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of one-sided specialization (intellectual completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: They are jealous of that abandonment to one special gift which really limits their capabilities... Philosophy serves culture... not by the fancied gift of absolute knowledge, but by suggesting questions which help one to detect the passion, and strangeness, and dramatic contrasts of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For practitioners: cultivate breadth and resist letting a single talent or theoretical system dominate the life or art; use theory as an instrument to expand perception rather than to negate parts of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy as instrument (theory should not sacrifice experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: The theory or idea or system which requires of us the sacrifice of any part of this experience... has no real claim upon us. 'Philosophy is the microscope of thought.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or using theories, check they illuminate experience rather than demand the exclusion of lived impressions. Theories should be judged instrumentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to fleeting impressions; resistance to habit
rubrics_metrics.description: To burn always with this hard, gemlike flame, to maintain this ecstasy, is success in life... Our failure is to form habits... Not to discriminate every moment some passionate attitude... is, on this short day of frost and sun, to sleep before evening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works and artistic practices that cultivate acute, ever-renewed attention to transient moments and impressions; anti-pattern is complacent habit or facile orthodoxy that dulls perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate poetic passion and multiplicity of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Great passions may give us this quickened sense of life... the poetic passion, the desire of beauty, the love of art for art's sake, has most; for art comes to you professing frankly to give nothing but the highest quality to your moments as they pass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the creator's devotion to beauty and to enriching momentary experience; artistic purpose that seeks intensification of moments (art for art's sake) is praised as a source of highest qualitative experience.
